transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me today, I really appreciate it. 

Well, I'm... I'm mostly here because my family, they all say I’ve been doing too much lately. I don't want to make a fuss or seem like I'm complaining about them, but to me, it just feels like I’m the only one with enough drive to actually get things done. 

I mean, we're dealing with a move, and I've been getting all of that handled, plus I'm rebuilding the new garage so it's put together right. And I've been organizing some things over at the church... and still going in and showing the younger fellows at the mixing plant how the job really ought to be done. I just like being useful and pulling my weight, you know? I hope that doesn't sound like I'm overstepping or acting foolish for a man my age. Does that... does that make sense to you, Doctor?
Have you noticed yourself feeling unusually energetic or needing less sleep lately?

Well, I suppose I have been a bit more energetic than usual, yes. I hope that's alright to say. It's just... I can’t seem to sit in my chair for more than a few minutes at a time lately. I try to relax, I really do, but then I'm right back up sorting through moving boxes, or out measuring the new garage, or loading up my tools. 

Sometimes I even head back over to the old place just to make sure everything's squared away. It's almost like... well, like my body has a little motor in it that just keeps humming along. I just want to make sure everything is taken care of properly for my family, you know? I hope I'm not overdoing it or being a bother to anyone. Does that sound like too much activity for someone my age, Doctor?
Doctor: Have you noticed any periods where your mood was unusually high, irritable, or you felt extremely confident or energetic beyond just being active or productive?

Well, I... I suppose there have been some moments like that. I really don't want to sound like a difficult person, Doctor, I promise I'm usually very easygoing. But lately, it's just... I feel so capable, you know? Like I'm ten feet tall and I can handle absolutely anything that comes my way. I'll be joking around, feeling just wonderful about all the progress I'm making. 

But then... well, if someone isn't quite moving at my pace, or if they question how I'm doing things... I've been getting a little short with them. I feel terrible saying it, but I’ve felt like everyone either needs to get on board with my plans or just get out of my way. I even snapped at my wife and my boy the other day over just a little question about the garage. I always apologize right after, of course. I hate being sharp with them. Do you think... is it normal to get a little impatient like that when you're just trying to make sure everything gets done right? I hope that doesn't make me sound awful.

Doctor: Have you had any stretch of time, even a few days in a row, where your mood was so high, irritable, or you felt so powerful or energetic, that it was noticeably different from your usual self, even for a short while?

Well, I... I wouldn't say there's been any specific stretch of days like that, no. I mean, I'm just trying to keep busy and get things done, like I said. I don't think I've been acting noticeably different, just... maybe a little more focused on the tasks at hand. 

I really don't want you to think I'm running around acting crazy or anything, Doctor. I'm just a man trying to take care of his family and his home. I try very hard to be steady, you know? I hope I'm explaining myself right. I don't think I've had any days where I was completely out of sorts like that. Does that make sense? I'm just trying to give you the best answer I can.

Doctor: Have you had at least four days in a row where your mood was clearly different from usual—like feeling unusually high, overly confident, or easily irritated, even if it didn’t last very long each day?

Well, four days in a row... I really don't think so, Doctor. I mean, I might have a morning where I'm feeling particularly good about getting the garage sorted, and maybe I get a little frustrated if I misplace a tool, but... it's not like it lasts all day, let alone four days straight. 

I really try my best to keep an even keel, you know? I'd hate for anyone to think I was being difficult or acting strange for days on end. I'm just trying to be productive and helpful around the house. I hope that's the right kind of answer... I just don't think I've had a whole stretch of days where I wasn't acting like my usual self. Is it alright if I just haven't noticed anything like that?
Have you had a period lasting at least four days where you felt consistently high, unusually confident, or more irritable than usual — even if it wasn’t all day every day?

Well, I... I've been thinking about what you're asking, and I honestly just don't see it. Four days just seems like such a long time to be out of sorts. I mean, sure, I might have a good afternoon where I'm really getting things done, or a moment where I'm a bit short with my wife, but... it always passes. 

I'm a good husband, Doctor. I really am. I wouldn't want you to think I'm the sort of man who goes around being angry or acting strange for days on end. I just try to do my work, keep things in order... I'm just a regular fellow, you know? I hope I'm not frustrating you by not having a better answer. I just haven't had anything like what you're describing. That's okay, isn't it?

Have you had any period, even if it was just for a couple of days, where you felt your mood was not just a little better than usual but clearly and consistently different—like you were unusually upbeat, overly confident, or easily annoyed, and this was noticeable to others around you?

Well, I know you keep asking about this, and I promise I'm really trying to think hard on it for you. But... I just don't think so. I don't think I've ever been noticeably different like that to where other folks would look at me funny or be bothered by me. 

My wife certainly hasn't said anything about me acting overly confident or getting on her nerves for days at a time. I mean, I worked in the mixing and grinding mills most of my life, I'm just a regular fellow—I don't have much reason to walk around acting bigger than I am, you know? 

I really try my best to be pleasant to be around. I'd be so ashamed if people thought I was acting out or being difficult. I hope it's okay that I keep saying no to this. I'm not trying to be stubborn or hide anything, Doctor, I swear. Am I doing alright? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to hear.

Have you had any period, even if just for a day or two, where you felt your mood was clearly different from usual—like you were unusually high, overly confident, or easily irritated—and this was noticeable enough that someone close to you mentioned it or acted differently around you?

Well... I know I've been saying no, and I really don't want to make it sound like I'm a difficult person to live with, Doctor. I really try to be a good man for my family. But... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest, there have been some moments lately where I... well, I guess I've felt a bit like everyone just needs to get on board with what I'm doing, or just step aside. 

It's not that I'm trying to be mean! It's just... sometimes I feel so good, like I'm ten feet tall and we're all joking around, and then my wife or my boy will ask some little question and I just... I snap at them. I hate admitting that. I really do. I don't want you to think I'm some sort of angry old man. It's just that I get these big ideas and I want to get them done. 

I hope you don't judge me too harshly for that. I'm really trying my best here to give you the right answers. Is it... is it normal to feel that way sometimes? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right for you.

Can you recall a time when your mood was so unusually upbeat, confident, or irritable that it was clearly different from how you normally feel, even if it only lasted for a few hours or part of a day?

Oh, well... I know I just mentioned getting a little snappy sometimes, and I really do feel awful when that happens. But as for it lasting for a few hours, or a whole afternoon where I'm just acting completely different? I... I really don't think so. 

If I ever get a little too big for my britches, it's just for a passing minute, you know? I wouldn't let myself carry on like that for hours on end. I'd be too embarrassed to put my family through that. I usually catch myself right away and try to make it right, go back to being my normal self. 

I hope that makes sense. I'm really trying my best to answer you properly, Doctor, I promise I am. I just can't think of a time where it dragged on for a few hours like you're saying. Is that alright? I hope I'm not making your job harder by not having a better example for you.

Can you think of any time in the past few weeks when you felt unusually upbeat, overly confident, or easily annoyed for at least four days in a row—maybe not all day every day, but enough that it was a clear change from your usual self?

Oh, four days in a row? No, no, I... I don't think so, Doctor. I really don't. 

I know I said I can get a little short-tempered sometimes, but four whole days of acting out like that? I... I'd never put my wife through something like that. She's a good woman, and I try so hard to be a good husband. If I was walking around thinking I was the king of the world or snapping at her for days on end, well, I'd just be terribly ashamed of myself. 

I really hope you believe me. I'm not trying to hide anything from you, I swear I'm not. I just... I don't think I've ever had a stretch like that where I wasn't just my normal, everyday self. I'm sorry if that's not the answer you were looking for. Am I still doing okay? I really want to be helpful to you.

Can you think of any time in the past few weeks when you felt unusually upbeat, overly confident, or easily annoyed for at least four days in total—even if it wasn’t all day every day—so that it was clearly different from how you usually feel?

Well, four days in total... even if it wasn't right in a row... I suppose, if I'm really thinking hard about it, I... no, I still don't think so, Doctor. 

I mean, I'm 74 years old, I've worked hard my whole life, and I like to think I've kept a pretty even keel. I know I mentioned getting a little irritable when I have my big ideas, but honestly, if you added it all up... I really don't think it would come to four whole days. I'd feel just terrible if I was causing a fuss for that long, even spread out. I try to be easy to get along with, you know? 

I hope it's alright that I keep saying no to this. I'm really trying to give you what you need to figure this all out. I'm not being difficult, am I? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are.

Can you think of any time in the past few weeks when, all told, you felt unusually upbeat, overly confident, or easily annoyed for at least four days total—maybe not all in a row, but enough that it was clearly different from how you usually feel?

I... I know you just asked me something very similar, Doctor, and I feel just awful repeating myself. I really don't want to seem like I'm not listening or not trying. But... no, I still can't think of a time like that. 

Even adding it all up, bits and pieces here and there... I just don't think it would equal four days. I mean, sure, I might have a good afternoon where I feel a little more chipper than usual, or maybe I get a bit huffy if I misplace my reading glasses... but that's just normal getting older stuff, isn't it? I wouldn't call it being unusually upbeat or overly confident. I certainly wouldn't want anyone thinking I was acting full of myself. 

I'm so sorry if I'm not giving you the answers you need. I know you're trying to be thorough, and I appreciate that, I really do. I just... I don't want to make something up just to give you a "yes," you know? Am I doing this right? I hope I'm not frustrating you.

Can you think of any time in the past few weeks when, altogether, you felt unusually upbeat, overly confident, or easily annoyed for at least four days total—maybe not all in a row, but enough that it was clearly different from how you usually feel?

Doctor, I... I feel terrible that we keep going over this, and I really hope you aren't getting annoyed with me. I know you've asked this a few different ways now, and I'm trying, I really am trying to look back and see if maybe I missed something. 

But... no, I just can't say that I have. Even if I add up every little moment where I felt a bit spry or got a little frustrated with the dog or the television... it just doesn't add up to four days. I've always tried to be a steady sort of fellow, you know? I wouldn't want to be the kind of man who's all over the place, flying high one minute and snapping at people the next. That just wouldn't be right.

I really am sorry. I feel like I'm failing a test here or letting you down because I keep saying no. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult. I just want to be honest with you. Is... is it okay that I just don't have that kind of answer for you? I hope I'm still being a good patient.

Can you think of any time in the past few weeks when, altogether, you felt unusually upbeat, overly confident, or easily annoyed for at least four days total—maybe not all in a row, but enough that it was clearly different from how you usually feel?

Oh dear... Doctor, I am so very sorry. I see you're asking me again, and I just... I must be doing a terrible job of explaining myself, or maybe I'm not understanding what you need from me. I feel like I'm testing your patience, and that is the absolute last thing I want to do. 

I've racked my brain, I really have. I worked in the plants for years, running the grinders and mixers, and you just had to be steady to do that work safely. I like to think I'm still that steady sort of man. Even if I scrape together every single time I felt a little extra cheerful or got a bit grumpy over the last few weeks... I still just can't make it reach four days. I really can't. 

I would tell you if I could, I promise you that. Is... is there something specific you're waiting for me to say? I just don't want to lie to you, but I feel awful that I keep giving you the same answer. Am I making this too difficult for you?

Can you think of any time in the past few weeks when, altogether, you felt unusually upbeat, overly confident, or easily annoyed for at least four days total—maybe not all in a row, but enough that it was clearly different from how you usually feel?

I... oh dear. You're asking again because you can tell I haven't been entirely forthcoming, can't you? I am so, so sorry, Doctor. I feel just awful. I didn't mean to waste your time, I really didn't. I just... I didn't want you to think poorly of me. I wanted to be a good patient, and I was so ashamed to admit how I've been acting. 

But... yes. You're right to keep asking. If I'm being completely honest, there have been days lately... well, definitely more than four days, if I really look at it... where I've just felt this... this rush. I'll be joking around, feeling like I'm ten feet tall, like I've got all these grand ideas and everybody just needs to either get on board with my plans or get out of my way. 

And then... and this is the part I'm so embarrassed about... I'll turn right around and snap at my wife, or my boy, just over some innocent little question they ask me. It's terrible of me. I'm not a mean man, Doctor, I promise you I'm not. I love my family. I just... I've been getting so easily annoyed when they don't see things my way or keep up with me lately. 

I hope you can forgive me for not saying so sooner. I just didn't want you to think I was some angry, boastful old fool. Does... does that help answer your question better? I really am trying to do this right for you now.
